verified_primary_sources.supports: BDD is collaborative discovery, formulation and automation around concrete examples; BDD is more than using Cucumber; examples lead into automated tests and implementation.
Step definition expression links Gherkin steps to executable code; Cucumber looks for a matching step definition; expression can be Cucumber Expression or regular expression.

Step text after the keyword is matched to step definition; keywords are not considered for matching; Scenario Outline/Examples define parameterized examples; Given/When/Then describe context/event/outcome.
Write test for next functionality, implement until pass, refactor; initial list of cases; refactoring maintains structure/behavior, and omitting it is a common TDD failure.
Properties, arbitraries/domains, generated and exhaustive inputs, stateful testing, data-driven properties, failure rerun and result shrinking modes/limits.

findings: Theory’s opening equates BDD with a ‘development of TDD toward business’; Cucumber’s primary BDD description emphasizes collaborative discovery, formulation, automation and concrete examples, and says BDD is more than Cucumber. This shorthand is an oversimplification, not an MCQ-key defect.

‘One same text serves as both requirement and test’ overstates the relation: collaborative examples can be formulated as executable specifications; not every Gherkin text automatically becomes a meaningful test. The theory later contains the correct step-definition explanation, but its broad opening conflicts with that nuance.
‘Сценарий ... обсуждается всей командой до кода’ is too absolute; BDD collaboration is continuous and roles collaborate, but not every scenario must be discussed by every team member.
Outline pricing example does not state the discount rule that yields 270/450/800, so expected totals are under-specified as a learning example.
Current examples/code plausibility not runtime-validated; no execution claimed.

Theory broadly agrees with Q9 key and Fowler sequence. It simplifies TDD to test then implementation and omits explicit observation of a meaningful red failure; the old correct option and explanation are more precise. Treat as a content-depth mismatch to consider, not a key defect.
Claims that TDD helps catch misunderstanding before production are reasonable but benefits should not be read as guarantees.
Opening calls PBT properties true for ‘any’ input and says the framework generates hundreds of random inputs; domain assumptions and generated/sample strategy are omitted.
Claims shrinking reduces to the ‘minimal’ reproducing example, which overstates the guarantee; jqwik shrinking has configurable modes/limits and does not promise a globally smallest counterexample.
Says three sorting properties cover infinitely many inputs; this is useful intuition only under stated domain and correct properties, not proof that an implementation is correct for all inputs.

‘PBT not suitable’ lists categorically UI, integration, business logic with fixed rules and E2E. These are overbroad prohibitions; applicability depends on whether useful properties/models and controllable environment exist.

jqwik database replay statement is version/configuration-specific and needs checking against 1.10.2 documentation before retaining. The user-guide’s rerun and failure persistence mechanisms are documented, but exact default filename/behavior should not be assumed from that general statement.
The Java sort example was inspected as prose/code, not compiled or run; no runtime claim made.
